_comment: QA-maintained defect log and issue register. Add product defects found in automated or manual runs here (type: Functional / Security / UI / Performance). generate_reports.py reads this file. Dates are DD-MMM-YYYY.

defects.title: Doc §4 cross-reference to 'section 1' for disabled Approvals is wrong
defects.description: Section 4 'Approval where required' says the Approvals screens are switched off '(see section 1)', but section 1 (Application Overview) contains no such statement.
defects.expected: Cross-reference points to the section that states which features are switched off, or section 1 lists them.
defects.actual: Section 1 has no mention of Approvals or CMDB Explorer being switched off.

defects.title: Problem ticket type missing from Ticket Types table; no number prefix defined
defects.description: §5.3 documents a Problem workflow, but §3 lists only Incident, Service Request and Change and states ticket numbers carry the INC/REQ/CHG prefixes. The live build has Problem tickets (PRB-000001 in the All open queue, 30-Oct-2026), yet the New ticket form offers staff only Incident / Service request / Change, and how a Problem is raised is not documented.
defects.expected: §3 lists Problem with its PRB prefix, default fields and how staff raise one.
defects.actual: PRB prefix exists in the application but not in the documentation; Problem cannot be raised from the New ticket form.

defects.title: Manager vs Team lead 'minor privileges' are not specified
defects.description: Doc §2 says the Manager differs from the Team lead only in 'a few minor privileges' without listing them, so the difference cannot be verified.
defects.expected: Role matrix lists every privilege that differs between Team lead and Manager.
defects.actual: Not specified; TC-RBAC-011 cannot be executed.

defects.title: Customer visibility default may expose colleagues' tickets
defects.description: By default a Customer sees the other tickets of their own company account (workspace setting). Incidents can contain sensitive data (e.g. access requests, personal issues). Confirm this default is intended and approved by the data owner.
defects.expected: Product owner confirms the default (or switches it off by default) and the setting is documented in the admin guide.
defects.actual: Default is ON per documentation; no privacy note.

defects.title: At-risk threshold: fixed 75% (ticket flow) vs per-policy threshold (Doc §6)
defects.found_in: Static review - ticket flow step 8 vs Doc §6
defects.description: The project ticket flow states the at-risk alert fires at 75%; Doc §6 says the threshold is set per policy. Test expectations are baselined at 75% for both Standard and Premium.
defects.expected: Confirm the configured threshold for each policy.

defects.title: Auto-close '5 days' - calendar vs business days not specified
defects.found_in: Static review - Doc §4, ticket flow step 10
defects.description: Resolved tickets close automatically after five days (checked hourly). Whether this is calendar days or business days, and the acceptable delay after the 5-day mark (up to 1 hour), is not stated.
defects.expected: Rule states calendar/business days and tolerance.
defects.actual: Unspecified; boundary test TC-INC-010 assumes calendar days with up to 1 hour delay.

defects.title: Ticket flow implies an SLA timer for every ticket; Doc §4 says Changes have no SLA
defects.found_in: Static review - ticket flow step 3 vs Doc §4
defects.description: Ticket flow step 3 ('SLA timer starts') does not exclude Changes; Doc §4 states Changes have no SLA in the default setup. Tests follow Doc §4.
defects.expected: Both sources state that Changes have no SLA by default.

defects.title: Field limits not documented (subject length, attachment types and size)
defects.description: Maximum subject length and allowed attachment types / maximum size are not documented, so boundary tests cannot have exact expected results.

defects.title: Flow diagram and test credential list still use old role names
defects.found_in: Static review - Doc §5 figure; project credential list
defects.description: The ticket-to-support-team figure uses 'Agent' and 'Manager'. The credential list shared with QA is mislabelled: verified on the live build (JWT role claim, 30-Oct-2026) sakthibalaji.m ('Customer') is an employee, saraswathi.karunanidhi ('Agent') is a team_lead, and sivasrigananapathi.sundaram ('Admin' and 'Manager') is a manager.
defects.expected: Figure and credential list use current role names and each login's real role.
defects.actual: Mislabelled credentials; no customer or Super admin login was actually supplied (see ISS-002).

defects.title: Avg first response display format above one hour not specified
defects.description: Doc §8 says Avg first response is shown in minutes when under one hour, but not how it is shown at or above one hour.
defects.expected: Format defined for both ranges (e.g. 'h m').
defects.actual: Only the under-one-hour format is defined.

defects.title: Access token stored in localStorage instead of an HttpOnly cookie
defects.found_in: Live build, 30-Oct-2026 - browser storage inspection after sign-in (all three roles)
defects.description: After sign-in the application sets no cookies; the JWT access token (and user profile) is kept in localStorage under 'opsdesk.auth'. Any script running on the page can read it, so a single XSS flaw would let an attacker steal sessions.
defects.expected: Session carried in a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie (or tokens held in memory with a refresh cookie), not readable by page scripts.
defects.actual: localStorage key 'opsdesk.auth' holds a readable JWT (claims include user_id, tid, role); context.cookies() returns [].

defects.title: 'Declare Major Incident' offered on a Service Request
defects.found_in: Live build, 30-Oct-2026 - REQ-000005 opened as Manager
defects.description: The Major Incident Workflow banner with a 'Declare Major Incident' button, and the 'Major incident' checkbox, are shown on service request REQ-000005 (P4). Major incidents apply to Incidents (Doc §2, §8); declaring one on a request would put it in the Major incidents queue and the Major Incidents report.
defects.expected: Major-incident controls appear on Incident tickets only.
defects.actual: Controls are shown on a Service Request.

defects.title: Opening /admin without permission silently shows a ticket queue
defects.found_in: Live build, 30-Oct-2026 - Employee, Team lead and Manager opening /admin
defects.description: Administration is correctly refused, but the user gets no message: the URL stays /admin and the 'Assigned to me' queue is rendered instead.
defects.expected: A clear 'You do not have access to Administration' message, or a redirect that changes the URL.
defects.actual: URL /admin with the 'Assigned to me' queue and no explanation.

defects.title: Employees are shown an 'Unassigned' queue they can never use
defects.description: Employees correctly cannot see unassigned tickets, but the sidebar still lists an 'Unassigned' queue for them, which always reads 0 even when the Manager's Unassigned queue has tickets.
defects.expected: Queue hidden for Employees (Doc §2: unassigned tickets are not visible to them).
defects.actual: 'Unassigned 0' link shown; opening it shows 'Nothing here'.

issues.title: Application URL unreachable - ngrok endpoint offline (ERR_NGROK_3200)
issues.impact: Blocks all test execution (automated and manual).
issues.action: Restart the tunnel (or provide a stable staging URL) and share the URL; update OPSDESK_BASE_URL in automation/.env.

issues.title: No Customer and no Super admin login - supplied credentials are mislabelled
issues.impact: Verified roles: sakthibalaji.m = employee (supplied as Customer), saraswathi.karunanidhi = team_lead (supplied as Agent), sivasrigananapathi.sundaram = manager. All customer-facing cases (25) and Administration / audit-log cases (14) are blocked.
issues.action: Provide a real customer login (customer of one account, e.g. Globex Retail) and Super admin access for the test workspace; add them to automation/fixture/users.json.

issues.title: Approvals partly live despite being documented as switched off; CMDB Explorer off
issues.impact: Live build shows 'Send for approval', an 'Awaiting approval' state (SLA paused) and 'Approved - fulfil' / 'Reject' actions (REQ-000005). Approval cases WAIT-004 and REQ-005/006 can be run manually; multi-approver rules (REQ-007) and CHG-005 remain unclear.
issues.action: Confirm these are deferred to a later release and formally descope, or enable them in the test workspace.

issues.title: Inbound channel endpoints not provided (email, WhatsApp, monitoring, API)
issues.impact: Channel intake cases (CHN-001..006) and notification checks cannot run.
issues.action: Share the inbound mailbox / webhook / API details and a test mailbox QA can read.

issues.title: Automation locators calibrated against the live UI
issues.impact: Locators, routes and test data were re-mapped to the live build on 30-Oct-2026 (sidebar links, ticket row buttons, header actions, property selects, exports on the Dashboard). Data-creating scenarios still need their first live run.
issues.action: Run data-creating scenarios once approved (they create QA-AUTO tickets and notify the assignee).

issues.title: Shared environment: other people are working with the same accounts during testing
issues.impact: Tickets change state while being tested (e.g. INC-000009 was resolved and closed between two checks on 30-Oct-2026), and queue counts move. Count-based and data-dependent checks can give false results.
issues.action: Give QA dedicated test accounts, or agree a test window; automation uses its own QA-AUTO tickets to limit interference.
